name: Apple (Fruit)
visual_anchor: A shiny red apple with a green leaf on its stem, resting on a wooden table beside a basket of more apples, bright morning light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round, crunchy fruit that can be red, green or yellow
Grows on trees in orchards and is picked in autumn
Has a core with small brown seeds in the middle
Belongs to the rose family of plants

facts_and_myths.claim: Apples float in water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: About a quarter of an apple is air, which makes it light enough to float.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are more than 7,500 different kinds of apples grown around the world.

facts_and_myths.claim: Swallowing an apple seed makes an apple tree grow in your tummy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Seeds need soil, sunlight and time to sprout. A swallowed seed simply passes through your body.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Apple trees grow from seeds, but farmers usually grow new ones by joining branches onto roots.

name: Banana
visual_anchor: A bright yellow bunch of bananas hanging from a big green banana plant in a sunny tropical garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long, curved yellow fruit that you peel before eating
Grows in big hanging bunches called hands
Turns from green to yellow to brown-speckled as it ripens
Botanists actually call it a berry

facts_and_myths.claim: A banana is a kind of berry.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Botanists call a fruit a berry when it grows from one flower and has seeds inside. Bananas fit that rule.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bananas curve because they grow upward toward the sunlight.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bananas grow on tall wooden trees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The banana plant is a giant herb. Its trunk is made of tightly rolled leaves, not wood.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A banana plant can grow taller than a grown-up in less than a year.

name: Strawberry
visual_anchor: Plump red strawberries with green leafy tops growing on a low plant in a sunny garden patch, close-up, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, sweet, heart-shaped red fruit
Has a leafy green cap on top
Tiny yellow seeds dot its outside
Grows on low plants that send out runners

facts_and_myths.claim: One strawberry carries about 200 tiny seeds on its outside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Those little yellow specks on the skin are the seeds, and an average strawberry has around 200.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Strawberry plants spread by sending out runners that grow brand-new baby plants.

facts_and_myths.claim: Strawberries are true berries.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Botanists do not count strawberries as berries, because their seeds sit on the outside.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Each little seed on a strawberry is actually a tiny fruit of its own.

name: Watermelon
visual_anchor: A big striped green watermelon cut open to show its juicy red inside and black seeds, on a picnic blanket in summer sunshine, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge fruit with a green striped rind
Juicy red or pink inside with black seeds
A favorite cool snack on hot summer days
Belongs to the same plant family as cucumbers and pumpkins

facts_and_myths.claim: A watermelon is about 92 percent water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most of a watermelon is water, which is why it tastes so juicy and refreshing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Japan, some farmers grow cube-shaped watermelons inside square boxes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Swallowing watermelon seeds makes a watermelon grow in your stomach.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Seeds cannot sprout inside your body. They just pass through without growing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some watermelons have yellow flesh instead of red.

name: Mango
visual_anchor: Ripe mangoes glowing yellow, orange and red hanging from a leafy mango tree in a sunny tropical orchard, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sweet tropical fruit with juicy orange-yellow flesh
Has one big flat seed in the middle
Grows on tall evergreen trees in warm countries
The national fruit of India

facts_and_myths.claim: Mangoes are related to cashews and pistachios.
facts_and_myths.explanation: All three come from plants in the same family, called the cashew family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mango trees can keep growing fruit for more than 100 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: A ripe mango always has red skin.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many ripe mangoes stay green or yellow. A gentle squeeze and a sweet smell show ripeness better.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are hundreds of kinds of mangoes grown around the world.

name: Pineapple
visual_anchor: A golden pineapple with a spiky green crown growing in the middle of a low leafy plant on a sunny farm, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tropical fruit with rough, scaly golden skin
Wears a spiky crown of green leaves
Grows from the middle of a low plant on the ground
Is really many small fruits joined together

facts_and_myths.claim: A pineapple takes about two years to grow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A pineapple plant usually needs around 18 months to two years to grow one fruit.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: You can grow a new pineapple plant from the leafy top of one.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pineapples grow high up on trees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Each pineapple grows from the center of a short, spiky plant close to the ground.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pineapple has a natural helper called bromelain that can make your tongue tingle.

name: Orange
visual_anchor: Bright round oranges hanging among glossy green leaves and white blossoms on an orange tree, sunny blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round citrus fruit with a bumpy, peelable skin
Inside is split into juicy segments
Famous for vitamin C and fresh juice
Shares its name with a color

facts_and_myths.claim: The color orange was named after the fruit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: People named the fruit first. Later, the word was also used for its bright color.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Orange trees can have sweet-smelling flowers and ripe fruit at the same time.

facts_and_myths.claim: A ripe orange always has orange skin.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In warm tropical places, ripe oranges often stay green because cool nights help the orange color appear.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Most oranges have about ten segments inside.

name: Grapes
visual_anchor: Clusters of plump purple and green grapes hanging from a leafy vine in a sunny countryside vineyard, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small round fruits that grow in bunches
Can be green, red or dark purple
Grow on climbing vines
Become raisins when they are dried

facts_and_myths.claim: Raisins are dried grapes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When grapes dry in the sun or in machines, they shrink and turn into sweet, chewy raisins.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Grapevines climb by wrapping curly tendrils around anything they can reach.

facts_and_myths.claim: Grapes are a healthy snack for dogs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Grapes and raisins can make dogs very sick. Keep them away from pets and ask an adult about pet treats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some grapes are grown to be seedless, so you can eat them whole.

name: Cherry
visual_anchor: Pairs of glossy dark red cherries on long green stems hanging from a leafy branch in a sunny orchard, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, round, shiny red fruit
Often hangs in pairs on long thin stems
Has one hard stone in the middle that you should not eat
A stone fruit related to plums and peaches

facts_and_myths.claim: Cherries are closely related to plums and peaches.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are all stone fruits, with soft flesh around one hard pit, and grow on related trees.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Traverse City in Michigan calls itself the Cherry Capital of the World.

facts_and_myths.claim: Every cherry blossom tree grows tasty cherries.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many cherry blossom trees are grown just for flowers and make tiny sour fruit or none at all.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sweet cherries and sour cherries come from two different kinds of cherry trees.

name: Kiwi Fruit
visual_anchor: A fuzzy brown kiwi fruit cut in half showing bright green flesh, a ring of tiny black seeds and a pale center, on a white plate, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small oval fruit with fuzzy brown skin
Bright green inside with tiny black seeds
Grows on climbing woody vines
Shares its name with a famous New Zealand bird

facts_and_myths.claim: This fruit was named after the kiwi bird.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Farmers in New Zealand gave it the name because its small, fuzzy brown shape looks like the bird.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The fuzzy skin of a kiwi fruit is safe to eat after it is washed.

facts_and_myths.claim: Kiwi fruit first came from New Zealand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The fruit is originally from China. New Zealand made it famous around the world.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Golden kiwi fruits have smooth skin and yellow flesh.

name: Dragon Fruit
visual_anchor: A bright pink dragon fruit with green-tipped scales, cut open to show white flesh with tiny black seeds, on a sunny tropical market table, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Hot pink fruit with green flame-like scales
White or red inside with many tiny black seeds
Grows on a climbing cactus
Its large flowers bloom only at night

facts_and_myths.claim: Dragon fruit grows on a cactus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It comes from a climbing cactus that clings to walls, posts and trees.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dragon fruit flowers open at night and usually close by the next morning.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dragon fruit first came from Asia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is native to Central and South America. Today it is also widely grown in Southeast Asia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some dragon fruits have bright magenta flesh instead of white.

name: Durian
visual_anchor: A large spiky green-brown durian split open to show creamy yellow pods inside, on a colorful Southeast Asian fruit stall, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big fruit covered in sharp, thorny spikes
Creamy yellow flesh inside
Famous for its very strong smell
Called the King of Fruits in Southeast Asia

facts_and_myths.claim: Durian is not allowed on Singapore's trains because of its smell.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its smell is so strong that signs on Singapore's trains show durian is not allowed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some people say durian smells stinky but tastes like sweet custard.

facts_and_myths.claim: Durian and jackfruit are the same fruit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They look a bit alike, but they grow on different trees from different plant families.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Durian spikes are so sharp that people often wear gloves to carry one.

name: Coconut
visual_anchor: Green coconuts clustered high up in a tall palm tree against a blue sky over a sandy tropical beach, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big round fruit with a hard, hairy brown shell
Has white flesh and clear water inside
Grows high up on palm trees near beaches
Can float across the ocean to new islands

facts_and_myths.claim: Coconuts can float across the ocean and grow on new islands.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their thick, airy husk keeps them afloat, so waves can carry them to faraway beaches.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A coconut has three little round eyes at one end.

facts_and_myths.claim: Coconut water and coconut milk are the same thing.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Coconut water is the clear liquid inside. Coconut milk is made by squeezing grated white flesh with water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite its name, a coconut is not a true nut.

name: Lychee
visual_anchor: A bunch of bumpy pinkish-red lychees, one peeled to show pearly white flesh, on a bamboo tray in soft daylight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small round fruit with bumpy pink-red skin
Pearly white, juicy flesh inside
Has one shiny brown seed in the middle
Originally grown in southern China

facts_and_myths.claim: Lychees are related to rambutans and longans.
facts_and_myths.explanation: All three belong to the same plant family and have sweet white flesh around one seed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In ancient China, fresh lychees were treasured as a special treat for royalty.

facts_and_myths.claim: You should eat the bumpy red skin of a lychee.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Peel off the skin and spit out the seed. Only the white flesh is eaten.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lychee trees can grow taller than a two-story house.

name: Blueberry
visual_anchor: Clusters of dusty blue blueberries on a green bush with soft morning dew, close-up in a sunny garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny round fruit with deep blue skin
Grows in clusters on small bushes
Has a little crown shape on its top
Covered in a powdery coating called bloom

facts_and_myths.claim: Blueberries have a powdery coating that protects them.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The whitish dust, called bloom, is natural and helps keep the berry fresh.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America.

facts_and_myths.claim: Store-bought blueberries are bright blue on the inside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most farmed blueberries are pale green inside. Only some wild blueberries are blue all the way through.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Blueberries start out green and slowly turn blue as they ripen.

name: Pomegranate
visual_anchor: A round red pomegranate broken open to show hundreds of shiny ruby-red seeds, on a wooden board in warm light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round red fruit with a tough, leathery skin
Has a little crown on one end
Packed with hundreds of juicy red seeds
Its name means seeded apple

facts_and_myths.claim: The name pomegranate means seeded apple.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The name comes from old Latin words meaning apple and seeds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The juicy, jewel-like seeds of a pomegranate are called arils.

facts_and_myths.claim: Every pomegranate has exactly the same number of seeds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The number changes from fruit to fruit, from a few hundred to more than a thousand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pomegranate juice can stain clothes a deep red.

name: Papaya
visual_anchor: A ripe papaya cut in half lengthwise showing orange flesh and a center of shiny black seeds, beside a green papaya plant in sunshine, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long tropical fruit with soft orange flesh
Has a hollow center full of round black seeds
Grows in clusters under the leaves of a tall, slim plant
Contains a natural helper that softens meat

facts_and_myths.claim: Papaya contains something that can make meat tender.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Papaya has a natural helper called papain that breaks down tough meat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Green, unripe papaya is shredded to make crunchy salads in Southeast Asia.

facts_and_myths.claim: Papaya plants take many years before they grow fruit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Papaya plants grow fast and can make fruit within about a year.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A papaya plant looks like a tree, but its stem is soft and not really woody.

name: Avocado
visual_anchor: An avocado cut in half showing creamy green flesh and a big round brown seed, on a cutting board in a bright kitchen, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Pear-shaped fruit with bumpy dark green skin
Creamy, buttery green flesh inside
Has one big round seed in the middle
The main ingredient in guacamole

facts_and_myths.claim: Avocados only ripen after they are picked from the tree.
facts_and_myths.explanation: An avocado stays hard on the tree and softens a few days after it is picked.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Avocados were once nicknamed alligator pears because of their bumpy green skin.

facts_and_myths.claim: An avocado is a vegetable.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Avocados grow from flowers and hold a seed, so they are fruits.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Botanists call an avocado a large berry with a single seed.

name: Carrot
visual_anchor: Bright orange carrots with feathery green tops freshly pulled from rich brown garden soil, sunny afternoon, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long, crunchy orange vegetable
Has feathery green leaves on top
Grows under the ground as a root
A favorite snack for rabbits in cartoons

facts_and_myths.claim: The first farmed carrots were purple or yellow, not orange.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Orange carrots became popular later, after farmers in the Netherlands grew them in the 1600s.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Carrot tops are leafy greens that can be cooked and eaten too.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eating carrots lets you see in the dark.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Carrots have vitamin A, which helps keep eyes healthy, but they cannot give you night vision.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Carrots also come in white, red and purple today.

name: Broccoli
visual_anchor: A fresh green head of broccoli with tiny tree-like florets on a wooden kitchen counter, bright and cheerful, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Green vegetable that looks like a tiny tree
Has a thick stalk and bumpy green tops called florets
The tops are actually lots of tiny flower buds
Comes from the same wild plant as cabbage and kale

facts_and_myths.claim: The part of broccoli we eat is made of flower buds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Each bumpy green floret is a cluster of buds that has not opened yet.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If broccoli is left to grow, it opens into little yellow flowers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Broccoli is a baby tree.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It only looks like a tiny tree. Broccoli is a leafy plant in the cabbage family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower and kale were all bred from one wild plant.

name: Tomato
visual_anchor: Juicy red tomatoes hanging in clusters on a leafy green vine in a sunny backyard garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round, juicy red food used in salads and sauces
Grows on leafy vines in gardens
The main ingredient in ketchup
Scientists call it a fruit, but cooks call it a vegetable

facts_and_myths.claim: Scientists call a tomato a fruit because it holds seeds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A fruit grows from a flower and carries seeds. Tomatoes do both, even though we cook them like vegetables.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: At the La Tomatina festival in Spain, people throw squashed tomatoes at each other for fun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tomatoes first came from Italy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tomatoes come from South America. They reached Italy only about 500 years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tomatoes also come in yellow, orange, green and even purple.

name: Potato
visual_anchor: A pile of round brown potatoes freshly dug from dark garden soil, with a little garden trowel nearby, warm sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Lumpy brown vegetable that grows underground
Used to make fries, chips and mashed dishes
Has little eyes that can sprout new shoots
First grown by farmers in the Andes of South America

facts_and_myths.claim: Potatoes were the first vegetable grown in space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In 1995, potato plants were grown on a NASA space shuttle as an experiment.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Green patches on potato skin are not safe to eat, so ask an adult to cut them away.

facts_and_myths.claim: A potato is a root.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A potato is a tuber, which is a swollen underground stem that stores food for the plant.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are thousands of potato varieties grown in Peru alone.

name: Corn
visual_anchor: A golden ear of corn with its green husk peeled back, standing in a tall sunny cornfield, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Rows of yellow kernels on a cob
Wrapped in green husks with silky threads on top
Grows on very tall stalks in big fields
One type pops into a fluffy movie snack

facts_and_myths.claim: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of rows.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kernel rows form in pairs as the cob grows, so the total is usually even.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Each silky thread on an ear of corn connects to one kernel.

facts_and_myths.claim: Corn kernels are always yellow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Corn can be white, red, blue, purple or even multicolored.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Popcorn pops because the water inside each kernel turns to steam.

name: Pumpkin
visual_anchor: Big round orange pumpkins with curly green vines sitting in a sunny autumn pumpkin patch, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big round orange squash with a thick stem
Grows on long, spreading vines
Carved into smiling jack-o'-lanterns for Halloween
Used to make a famous autumn pie

facts_and_myths.claim: Prize-winning giant pumpkins can weigh over 1,000 kilograms.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Growers raise special giant pumpkins for contests, and the biggest weigh more than a small car.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pumpkin flowers are bright yellow and can be cooked and eaten.

facts_and_myths.claim: All pumpkins are orange.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Some pumpkins are white, green, blue-gray or even striped.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pumpkins are in the same plant family as cucumbers and watermelons.

name: Cucumber
visual_anchor: Long green cucumbers hanging from a climbing vine with yellow flowers in a sunny garden, one sliced into cool round pieces, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long green vegetable with a cool, crunchy bite
Pale green inside with soft seeds
Grows on climbing vines with yellow flowers
Becomes a pickle when soaked in salty or sour liquid

facts_and_myths.claim: A cucumber is about 95 percent water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cucumbers are mostly water, which is why they feel so cool and crisp.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cucumbers belong to the same plant family as watermelons and pumpkins.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pickles grow on their own special pickle plant.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most pickles are cucumbers that have been soaked in salty water or vinegar.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because they hold seeds, cucumbers are fruits to a botanist.

name: Onion
visual_anchor: Golden-brown and purple onions on a wooden kitchen counter, one cut in half to show its rings of layers, bright daylight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round vegetable with papery brown, red or white skin
Made of many layers inside
Cutting it can make your eyes water
A close cousin of garlic and leeks

facts_and_myths.claim: Cutting an onion releases a gas that makes eyes water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Slicing an onion breaks its cells and lets out a gas that stings your eyes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The layers of an onion are actually special leaves that store food.

facts_and_myths.claim: Onions are a safe treat for dogs and cats.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Onions can make dogs and cats very sick. Always ask an adult before feeding pets people food.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: People in ancient Egypt grew and ate onions thousands of years ago.

name: Bell Pepper
visual_anchor: Shiny red, yellow, orange and green bell peppers lined up on a bright kitchen counter, colorful and cheerful, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Crunchy, hollow vegetable shaped a bit like a bell
Comes in green, yellow, orange and red
Has seeds clustered inside near the stem
A pepper with no spicy heat at all

facts_and_myths.claim: Red bell peppers have more vitamin C than oranges.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Weight for weight, a ripe red bell pepper holds more vitamin C than an orange.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bell peppers are not spicy because they lack capsaicin, which makes chili peppers hot.

facts_and_myths.claim: Green and red bell peppers always come from different plants.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many red peppers are green peppers left on the plant longer to ripen and change color.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Green bell peppers taste less sweet because they are picked before ripening.

name: Eggplant
visual_anchor: Glossy deep purple eggplants with green caps hanging from a leafy plant with lilac flowers in a sunny garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Shiny, deep purple vegetable with a green cap
Soft, spongy pale flesh inside
Called aubergine in Britain
Named for early kinds that looked like white eggs

facts_and_myths.claim: Eggplants got their name from looking like eggs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early eggplants grown in Europe were small, white and egg-shaped.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Eggplants are in the same plant family as tomatoes and potatoes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eggplants are always purple.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Eggplants can be white, green, orange or striped, as well as purple.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: To a botanist, an eggplant is actually a berry.

name: Cabbage
visual_anchor: A round green cabbage and a purple-red cabbage sitting in a sunny vegetable garden with dewy leaves, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Round, leafy vegetable shaped like a ball
Leaves wrap tightly around each other
Comes in green, red-purple and napa varieties
Used to make sauerkraut and kimchi

facts_and_myths.claim: Red cabbage juice changes color when mixed with lemon juice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its natural purple coloring turns pink with sour liquids and blue-green with baking soda. Ask an adult to help.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Kimchi, a famous Korean side dish, is often made with napa cabbage.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cabbage and lettuce are the same kind of vegetable.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cabbage belongs to the mustard family with broccoli. Lettuce belongs to the daisy family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Brussels sprouts look like tiny cabbages and are close relatives.

name: Peas
visual_anchor: An open green pea pod showing a neat row of round bright green peas, on a climbing pea plant in a sunny garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, round, bright green vegetables
Grow lined up inside long green pods
Pea plants climb with thin curly tendrils
Helped a scientist discover how traits are passed down

facts_and_myths.claim: Gregor Mendel used pea plants to learn how traits pass to offspring.
facts_and_myths.explanation: By growing thousands of pea plants, he found patterns in how color and shape are inherited.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pea plants climb by wrapping thin curly tendrils around sticks and strings.

facts_and_myths.claim: Frozen peas are always much less healthy than fresh ones.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Peas are often frozen soon after picking, which helps them keep many of their nutrients.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Peas are legumes, part of the same plant family as beans and peanuts.

name: Sweet Potato
visual_anchor: Reddish-brown sweet potatoes on a rustic table, one cut open to show bright orange flesh, warm autumn light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long root vegetable with reddish-brown skin
Usually bright orange and sweet inside
Grows underground from a trailing vine
Related to morning glory flowers

facts_and_myths.claim: Sweet potatoes are related to morning glory flowers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sweet potatoes belong to the morning glory family, not the potato family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sweet potato leaves are cooked and eaten as greens in many countries.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sweet potatoes and yams are the same vegetable.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Real yams are a different plant with rough, bark-like skin, grown mostly in Africa and Asia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some sweet potatoes have purple or white flesh instead of orange.

name: Spinach
visual_anchor: A big bunch of fresh dark green spinach leaves in a garden basket under bright sunshine, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Leafy, dark green vegetable
Eaten raw in salads or cooked until soft
Shrinks a lot when it is cooked
Made famous by a cartoon sailor who gets super strong

facts_and_myths.claim: Spinach shrinks a lot when it is cooked.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Heat lets water escape from the leaves, so a big pile shrinks to a small bowl.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Crystal City, Texas, has a statue of Popeye and calls itself the Spinach Capital of the World.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eating spinach makes you super strong instantly, like Popeye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spinach is full of vitamins and minerals, but no food gives instant super strength.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spinach grows best in cool weather, like spring and autumn.

name: Sunflower
visual_anchor: Tall sunflowers with bright yellow petals and big brown centers standing in a field under a clear blue summer sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Very tall flower with bright yellow petals
Has a huge brown center full of seeds
Young buds turn to follow the sun across the sky
Its seeds are a popular snack and bird food

facts_and_myths.claim: A sunflower head is made of hundreds of tiny flowers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The big brown center is packed with tiny flowers, and each one can become a seed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sunflower seeds are arranged in neat spirals that follow a famous number pattern.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fully grown sunflowers turn to follow the sun all day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only young sunflowers track the sun. Grown-up sunflowers mostly stay facing east.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The sunflower is the state flower of Kansas.

name: Rose
visual_anchor: A bright red rose in full bloom with soft layered petals and green leaves in a sunny garden, gentle dewdrops, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Popular garden flower with soft, layered petals
Comes in red, pink, white, yellow and more
Has sharp prickles on its stem
Gives its family name to apples and strawberries

facts_and_myths.claim: Apples and strawberries are in the rose family.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Roses, apples, strawberries, cherries and pears are all members of the same plant family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: No rose in nature is truly blue.

facts_and_myths.claim: The sharp points on rose stems are true thorns.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Botanists call them prickles, because they grow from the stem's outer skin, not from the wood.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The round fruits of rose plants are called rose hips.

name: Tulip
visual_anchor: Rows of red, yellow and pink tulips blooming in a colorful spring field with a windmill far away, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Spring flower shaped like a cup
Grows from a bulb planted in autumn
Comes in almost every color
Famous for colorful fields in the Netherlands

facts_and_myths.claim: Tulips keep growing in a vase after they are cut.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cut tulip stems can keep stretching taller and bending toward the light.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Keukenhof garden in the Netherlands plants about seven million flower bulbs each year.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tulips first came from the Netherlands.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wild tulips come from Central Asia. They were brought to Europe through Turkey.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tulip petals close up at night and open again in the sunshine.

name: Lotus Flower
visual_anchor: A pink lotus flower rising above a calm pond on a tall stem, surrounded by big round green leaves, soft morning light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Pink or white flower growing in ponds
Rises on a tall stem high above the water
Big round leaves that water rolls right off
The national flower of India

facts_and_myths.claim: Lotus leaves stay clean because water and dirt roll right off.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tiny bumps on the leaves make water bead up and carry away dirt. Scientists call this the lotus effect.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists once sprouted a lotus seed that was more than 1,000 years old.

facts_and_myths.claim: A lotus and a water lily are the same plant.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are different plants. Water lilies float on the water, while lotus flowers rise high above it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lotus seed pods look like showerheads full of little holes.

name: Cherry Blossom
visual_anchor: A tree covered in fluffy pale pink cherry blossoms with petals drifting down over a park path in spring sunshine, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Soft pink or white flowers that cover whole trees
Blooms in early spring for only a short time
Petals fall like gentle pink snow
A famous symbol of spring in Japan

facts_and_myths.claim: In 1912, Tokyo gave Washington, D.C. thousands of cherry trees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: More than 3,000 trees were sent as a gift of friendship, and they still bloom every spring.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Japan, families enjoy flower-viewing picnics called hanami under the blossoms.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cherry blossoms stay on the trees for many months.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The blossoms usually last only about one or two weeks before the petals fall.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Weather experts in Japan forecast when the cherry blossoms will bloom.

name: Common Daisy
visual_anchor: Little white daisies with sunny yellow centers dotting a green lawn on a bright spring morning, close-up, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small flower with white petals and a yellow center
Pops up in lawns and meadows
Closes at night and opens in the morning
Its name comes from the words day's eye

facts_and_myths.claim: The name daisy comes from the words day's eye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Daisies open in the morning and close at night, like an eye opening for the day.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The common daisy is a close relative of sunflowers.

facts_and_myths.claim: A daisy is just one single flower.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Each daisy head is many tiny flowers packed together, both in the white ring and the yellow center.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Children often weave daisies together into flower chains.

name: Orchid
visual_anchor: Elegant purple and white orchid flowers on a long arching stem in a pot by a sunny window, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Elegant flower with fancy, unusual petal shapes
Often grown as a houseplant in pots
Many wild kinds cling to tree branches
One kind gives us the vanilla flavor

facts_and_myths.claim: Vanilla comes from a kind of orchid.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vanilla flavor comes from the seed pods of a climbing orchid plant.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Orchid seeds are so tiny that they look like dust.

facts_and_myths.claim: Orchids only grow in hot tropical jungles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Orchids grow on every continent except Antarctica, including cool forests and meadows.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The orchid family is one of the largest flower families, with tens of thousands of kinds.

name: Lavender
visual_anchor: Long rows of purple lavender stretching across a sunny countryside field with bees buzzing around the blossoms, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Thin stalks topped with tiny purple flowers
Has a sweet, calming smell
Used in soaps, lotions and scented bags
Grows in famous purple fields in southern France

facts_and_myths.claim: Bees love visiting lavender flowers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lavender is full of sweet nectar, so bees and butterflies visit it all summer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lavender belongs to the mint family, along with basil and rosemary.

facts_and_myths.claim: Lavender only comes in purple.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most lavender is purple, but some kinds have white or pink flowers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The color lavender, a pale purple, is named after this plant.

name: Dandelion
visual_anchor: A fluffy white dandelion seed head with tiny seeds floating away on the breeze, beside a bright yellow dandelion flower on green grass, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, bright yellow flower found in lawns
Turns into a fluffy white ball of seeds
Children blow on it to send the seeds flying
Its name means lion's tooth

facts_and_myths.claim: Each dandelion seed has its own tiny parachute.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fluffy white hairs on every seed catch the wind and carry it far away.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name dandelion comes from French words meaning lion's tooth, after its jagged leaves.

facts_and_myths.claim: Blowing a dandelion puffball tells you the real time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Counting puffs is just a fun game. The seeds are simply floating away to grow somewhere new.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bees visit dandelions early in spring when few other flowers are open.

name: Venus Flytrap
visual_anchor: A cheerful green Venus flytrap with open red-lined traps and little spiky edges, in a pot on a sunny windowsill, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small plant with leaves shaped like open jaws
Its traps snap shut when touched in the right way
Catches insects and spiders for extra food
Grows in the wild only in North and South Carolina

facts_and_myths.claim: The trap closes only when tiny hairs inside are touched twice quickly.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Needing two touches helps the plant avoid closing on raindrops or falling bits.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the wild, Venus flytraps grow only in a small area of the Carolinas.

facts_and_myths.claim: Venus flytraps can catch and eat big animals like mice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The traps are small and mostly catch insects and spiders. The plant also makes food from sunlight.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A Venus flytrap trap can snap shut in less than a second.

name: Hibiscus
visual_anchor: A large bright red hibiscus flower with a long center stalk, surrounded by glossy green leaves in a sunny tropical garden, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large, colorful trumpet-shaped tropical flower
Has a long stalk poking out of its center
Often tucked behind the ear in Hawaii
The national flower of Malaysia

facts_and_myths.claim: A yellow hibiscus is the state flower of Hawaii.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hawaii chose a native yellow hibiscus as its official state flower.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some hibiscus petals are used to make a bright red, tangy tea.

facts_and_myths.claim: A single hibiscus flower stays open for weeks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most hibiscus blooms last only about a day, but the plant keeps making new ones.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hibiscus is the national flower of Malaysia.

name: Marigold
visual_anchor: Bright orange and golden marigold flowers with ruffled petals growing in a sunny vegetable garden bed, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Ruffled flower in bright orange and golden yellow
Has a strong, spicy smell
Strung into colorful garlands for festivals in India
Gardeners plant it near vegetables to help keep pests away

facts_and_myths.claim: Gardeners plant marigolds near vegetables to help keep some pests away.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Marigolds have a strong smell, and many gardeners grow them as helper plants beside vegetables.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: French and African marigolds actually first came from Mexico and Central America.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pot marigolds and French marigolds are the same plant.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They share a name but are different plants. Pot marigold is also called calendula.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Marigold garlands brighten many Diwali celebrations in India.

name: Baobab Tree
visual_anchor: A giant baobab tree with a thick bottle-shaped trunk and short root-like branches standing on a golden African savanna at sunset, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge tree with a very wide, bottle-shaped trunk
Its bare branches look like roots in the air
Stores lots of water inside its trunk
Grows in Africa, Madagascar and Australia

facts_and_myths.claim: A baobab tree stores water inside its giant trunk.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its spongy trunk soaks up water in the rainy season to survive long dry months.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Baobab trees appear in the famous story The Little Prince.

facts_and_myths.claim: Baobab trees really grow upside down.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They only look upside down because their bare branches resemble roots. Their real roots are underground.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some baobab trees are more than 1,000 years old.

name: Giant Sequoia
visual_anchor: Enormous reddish-brown giant sequoia trunks towering over a sunny forest trail in California with tiny hikers looking up in wonder, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Enormous tree with thick reddish-brown bark
Grows in the mountains of California
Can live for thousands of years
The biggest tree on Earth by total size

facts_and_myths.claim: A giant sequoia named General Sherman is the world's largest tree by volume.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It grows in Sequoia National Park and has more wood than any other single tree.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Giant sequoia bark can be thick and spongy, which helps protect it from forest fires.

facts_and_myths.claim: The giant sequoia is the world's tallest tree.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is the biggest overall, but the tallest trees are coast redwoods, its close cousins.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Giant sequoia cones are surprisingly small, about the size of a chicken egg.

name: Oak Tree
visual_anchor: A wide, leafy oak tree with a sturdy trunk in a sunny meadow, with a squirrel holding an acorn on a low branch, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large, strong tree with wavy-edged leaves
Grows nuts called acorns with little caps
Squirrels love to collect its nuts
Its hard wood is used for furniture and barrels

facts_and_myths.claim: Squirrels help plant new oak trees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Squirrels bury acorns to eat later, and the ones they forget can sprout into new oaks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A big oak tree can make thousands of acorns in a good year.

facts_and_myths.claim: Young oak trees grow acorns in their very first year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most oak trees need about 20 years or more before they start making acorns.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some oak trees live for hundreds of years.

name: Bamboo
visual_anchor: A tall green bamboo forest with smooth jointed stalks reaching toward soft sunlight, a peaceful path winding between them, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tall green stalks with rings called joints
Hollow inside like a tube
The favorite food of giant pandas
Actually a giant grass, not a tree

facts_and_myths.claim: Some bamboo can grow almost a meter in one day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Certain kinds of bamboo are among the fastest-growing plants in the world.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some bamboo kinds flower all at the same time only once every few decades.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bamboo is a kind of tree.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bamboo looks like a tree, but it is really a giant member of the grass family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bamboo is strong enough to build houses, bridges and bicycles.

name: Saguaro Cactus
visual_anchor: A tall green saguaro cactus with raised arms standing in a sunny desert with orange rocks and a bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tall desert cactus with arms that point upward
Covered in sharp spines
Swells up to store rainwater
Grows in the Sonoran Desert of Arizona and Mexico

facts_and_myths.claim: Woodpeckers make nest holes inside saguaro cactuses.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gila woodpeckers peck holes in the cactus, and later other birds like owls move in.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A saguaro may take around 50 years or more to grow its first arm.

facts_and_myths.claim: You can drink water straight from a saguaro cactus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The juice inside is not safe to drink and can make you sick. In the desert, carry your own water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The saguaro's white flower is the state wildflower of Arizona.

name: Maple Tree
visual_anchor: A maple tree glowing with bright red and orange autumn leaves, with leaves drifting onto a grassy park, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tree with pointy, hand-shaped leaves
Leaves turn brilliant red and orange in autumn
Its seeds spin like little helicopters
Its leaf appears on the flag of Canada

facts_and_myths.claim: About 40 liters of maple sap make just 1 liter of syrup.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Maple sap is very watery, so it is boiled for a long time to make thick syrup.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Maple seeds have wings that spin like helicopter blades as they fall.

facts_and_myths.claim: Maple syrup comes from the tree's leaves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Syrup is made from sap collected from the trunk in late winter and early spring.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A red maple leaf is the symbol in the middle of Canada's flag.

name: Palm Tree
visual_anchor: Tall palm trees with feathery green fronds swaying over a white sandy beach and turquoise sea on a sunny day, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tall, thin trunk with no branches
Big feathery or fan-shaped leaves at the very top
Grows on sunny beaches and in deserts
Some kinds give us coconuts and dates

facts_and_myths.claim: The big leaves of a palm tree are called fronds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Palm leaves are called fronds, and they grow from the top of the trunk.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Dubai, people built islands shaped like a giant palm tree.

facts_and_myths.claim: Palm trees are woody trees just like oaks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Palms are more closely related to grasses. Their trunks do not grow rings of wood like oaks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Date palms have been grown for their sweet fruit for thousands of years.

name: Banyan Tree
visual_anchor: A huge banyan tree with many hanging roots that have grown into pillar-like trunks, shading a sunny village square, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant shady tree with roots hanging from its branches
Its hanging roots grow down into new trunks
One tree can spread out like a small forest
The national tree of India

facts_and_myths.claim: The banyan is the national tree of India.
facts_and_myths.explanation: India chose the banyan because it is huge, long-living and gives lots of shade.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Great Banyan in Kolkata, India, looks like a whole forest but is one tree.

facts_and_myths.claim: A banyan tree has only one trunk.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Roots grow down from its branches, reach the ground and become many extra trunks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The banyan is a kind of fig tree.

name: Pine Tree
visual_anchor: A tall evergreen pine tree with long green needles and brown pine cones on a snowy mountainside under a bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Evergreen tree with long, thin needles
Makes woody cones that hold its seeds
Has a fresh, sticky sap
Some kinds live for thousands of years

facts_and_myths.claim: Pine cones open when dry and close when wet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The scales close up in damp weather to protect the seeds, then open when it is dry.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some bristlecone pine trees are more than 4,000 years old.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pine trees lose all their needles every winter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pines are evergreens. They drop old needles a few at a time and stay green all year.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pine needles usually grow in little bundles of two, three or five.

name: Fern
visual_anchor: Lush green ferns with feathery fronds and a curled-up young fiddlehead growing on a shady forest floor with soft sunbeams, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Leafy green plant with feathery fronds
Loves shady, damp forests
New leaves unroll from tight curls called fiddleheads
Makes tiny spores instead of flowers or seeds

facts_and_myths.claim: Ferns were growing on Earth before the dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fossils show ferns lived hundreds of millions of years ago, long before the first dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Young fern leaves unroll from curls that look like the top of a violin.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ferns grow from seeds like flowers do.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ferns never make flowers or seeds. They spread with tiny spores found under their leaves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some tree ferns can grow as tall as a house.

name: Aloe Vera
visual_anchor: A healthy aloe vera plant with thick, spiky green leaves growing in a clay pot on a sunny windowsill, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Succulent plant with thick, pointed green leaves
Has little soft spikes along its leaf edges
Its leaves are filled with a clear, slippery gel
The gel is often used to soothe sunburned skin

facts_and_myths.claim: Aloe vera gel is often used to soothe sunburns.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The cool gel from its leaves is used in many skin lotions. Ask an adult before using the plant itself.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Aloe vera stores water in its thick leaves, so it survives long dry spells.

facts_and_myths.claim: Aloe vera is a type of cactus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a succulent, but not a cactus. It belongs to a different plant family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Aloe vera plants grow tall spikes of yellow or orange flowers.

name: Rafflesia
visual_anchor: A giant reddish-orange rafflesia flower with five thick spotted petals resting on a mossy rainforest floor, lush green jungle around it, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Enormous red flower with big spotted petals
Grows in rainforests of Southeast Asia
Has no leaves, stems or roots of its own
The largest single flower in the world

facts_and_myths.claim: Rafflesia makes the largest single flower in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: One rafflesia flower can grow about as wide as a car tire.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rafflesia gives off a stinky smell like rotten meat to attract flies.

facts_and_myths.claim: Rafflesia has big green leaves to make food from sunlight.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It has no leaves at all. It takes all its food from a jungle vine it lives on.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A rafflesia bloom lasts only about a week before fading.
